Middle East.headline: OPT — Israeli military operation in central Gaza displaces families and threatens thousands
Middle East.body: Israeli forces launched a ground operation into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday, crossing the yellow line boundary along the Salah al-Din road for the first time since last October's ceasefire agreement. The movement forced displaced residents from their tents. Gaza’s Civil Defense warned that the ongoing offensive threatens more than 5,260 displaced Palestinians across six shelter sites, heightening risks of forced re-displacement and worsening humanitarian conditions amid severe emergency response shortages.
verified_figures: Over 5,260 displaced Palestinians threatened across six shelter sites

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Escalating violence kills 64 children and disrupts aid access in Taiz and Lahj
Middle East.body: Intensified hostilities in Yemen since 3 September have killed at least 64 children and injured 64 others, according to UNICEF. Clashes centered around densely populated areas in Taiz and Lahj provinces, alongside the growing isolation of Taiz City, are severely cutting off children from healthcare, safe water, food, and education. UNICEF warned child casualties are likely to rise as fighting persists near civilian areas, calling for immediate measures to protect civilians and halt hostilities.
verified_figures: At least 64 children killed since 3 September

Middle East.headline: Middle East — Reciprocal US and Iranian strikes target military sites in the Gulf and Iran
Middle East.body: Military tensions between Iran and the United States escalated in the Gulf following reciprocal strikes on strategic sites. Iranian forces carried out attacks targeting US military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait, including a US radar system in Bahrain and the Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait. US forces responded with airstrikes on Qeshm Island in southern Iran. The developments mark a notable acceleration of hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz, heightening risks of wider regional escalation.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Cholera outbreak kills over 800 people amid healthcare collapse
Middle East.body: A cholera epidemic across Yemen has killed at least 859 people, according to data from the World Health Organization. More than 116,700 suspected cholera cases have been recorded across 20 provinces. The World Health Organization warned that ongoing conflict has severely damaged the country's healthcare system, crippling the capacity of health institutions to manage the epidemic and treat infected populations.
verified_figures: Over 116,700 suspected cholera cases across 20 provinces

Americas.headline: Haiti: UN chief condemns Haiti attack that killed 47
Americas.body: At least 47 people, including at least five children, were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped by armed men in Haiti on Sunday, the United Nations confirmed on Tuesday. The incident, which took place in Kenscoff on the outskirts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in the troubled Caribbean country in recent years. In a video posted on social media, a gang leader threatened to murder hostages if Haiti's National Police kill any of his men in an attempt to rescue people. "If any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them," he said.

Americas.headline: Bukele confirms airstrike on Haitian gang leader Jeff's luxury mansion
Americas.body: The Salvadoran president welcomes the destruction of the home of Jeff Larose, one of Haiti's main crime leaders. It is not clear whether Jeff was in the building during the bombing. The president of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, confirmed on Wednesday that his forces had attacked and destroyed the luxurious mansion of one of the main leaders of Haiti's criminal gangs, known as "Jeff" Larose. For now, it is not clear whether the leader was killed in the strike or whether he was even in the house when it was bombed.

Americas.headline: Haitians Flood Streets in Celebration as Salvadoran Troops Arrive to Combat Gangs
Americas.body: In a moment of unexpected jubilation, thousands of Haitians filled the streets of Port-au-Prince on Tuesday to welcome the arrival of 2,500 Salvadoran soldiers dispatched to combat the rampant gang violence plaguing their nation. This surprising show of support for El Salvador's President, Nayib Bukele, was reported by the Associated Press. Waving Haitian flags and holding posters emblazoned with Bukele's image, demonstrators chanted his name, urging him not to abandon their cause. "Keep fighting... or they'll end up killing us all," read one sign. Others called for the deployment of explosive drones and robotic dogs to dismantle the armed groups. Africa.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a public health emergency of international concern, World Health Organization (WHO) chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said Wednesday. Europe.headline: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
Europe.body: - Published Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be "far more painful" than Kyiv's strikes, Vladimir Putin has vowed. In the early hours of Thursday, the double-arched, 12-mile bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea was hit for a third time this week. A combined missile-and-drone strike on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the bridge, collapsing part of it into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic. Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres
Asia-Pacific.body: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history. In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia. But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide. Asia-Pacific.headline: 28 Million in Poverty as Afghanistan Crisis Deepens Amid Returns, Drought and Aid Cuts
Asia-Pacific.body: The Kabul Tribune (KT) — The United Nations says Afghanistan’s humanitarian and economic crisis is worsening, with millions facing deepening poverty due to mass population returns, prolonged drought and declining international assistance. According to a new report by the United Nations Development Programme, an estimated 28 million people were living in poverty in Afghanistan in 2025. The situation has been compounded by the return of approximately 2.9 million Afghans during the year, pushing an additional 1.4 million people into hardship. Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Some residents of Gwagwa community in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC) of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) are still relying on river water for domestic use, including drinking, despite the recent suspected cholera outbreak allegedly linked to the community’s water sources. Abuja Metro gathered that the recent outbreak has claimed nine lives, according to the councilor representing the area, Nuhu Aliyu Usman, who confirmed the figure in a telephone interview yesterday.
